decisions.reason: The candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY covering the accepted gravity-fed solenoid path and absence of retained matcha in the spout or tubing.
The candidate already has a same-message MODIFY establishing the solenoid valve and press-to-open, release-to-stop control behavior.
The existing same-message MODIFY already requires the wiring plan to cover solenoid power, control wiring, and station-button actuation.
The existing same-message MODIFY already adds the solenoid valve and station-button control hardware to the BOM obligations.

The accepted spout appearance, stainless-steel material, and custom fabrication are already represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY; the valve placement does not require another spout-design attribute.
The solenoid layout decision does not alter the placard requirement, while the separate placard clause in the source message is already represented by its own same-message MODIFY.
Adopting the solenoid dispensing path does not necessarily change the existing requirement that the spout be removable or easy to flush and clean.
The accepted valve placement does not modify or remove the existing requirement for a seal that prevents leakage into the base.
The stainless-steel spout material accepted through the adjacent proposal is already represented by the candidate's same-message INTRODUCE; no additional material-state change is required.
The source decision does not establish any necessary change to enclosure thickness or maximum size.
The accepted dispensing layout has no effect on the machine's beige primary color or green accents.
The statement that the spout faces the baristas confirms the already-current orientation and does not change candidate state.
